# Hiring Manager Screen

[← Airbnb](../README.md) · [Every Airbnb question](../../airbnb.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/hiring-manager-screen)

`deep-dive` `fit`

---

## Requirements

- A 45-minute video conversation with the prospective hiring manager.
- The manager explains the position, the team, and the roadmap currently in progress.
- The candidate should:
  - Summarize their background in 5–10 minutes, focusing on resume highlights rather than a complete deep dive.
  - Cover two or three projects at an elevator-pitch level.
  - Raise 3–5 meaningful questions about the team, responsibilities, and path for growth.
- This stage produces a binary team-fit signal for the team-match pool.

## Notes

- Multiple candidates say they waited for weeks without hearing back after conversations that seemed positive — passing this stage is a gate, not an automatic progression.
- A frequent rejection explanation is that a better-matched candidate was already progressing; the discussion effectively compares background-to-team fit with the particular needs of the open requisition.
- The candidate's questions are at least as important as their responses. Broad prompts such as "what is the team culture" tend to perform worse than targeted ones such as "how is the team approaching headcount in the era of AI tools?"
- A well-rounded question list addresses: organizational and team structure, recent accomplishments, largest unresolved challenges, role boundaries, internal tools, and progression from senior to staff.
- The manager can screen someone out at this point if the apparent experience scope falls short of the requisition's expectations — this is the stage most likely to reveal a downlevel offer.
- This discussion can occasionally be the opening stage, ahead of the onsite. Even excellent rapport with the hiring manager guarantees nothing: an internal transfer may fill the requisition, leading to redirection to another team within the same organization or an immediate move to a virtual onsite that may have an unusual format.

## Preparation

- Prepare and practice both a five-minute introduction to your background and a 30-second version.
- Create a focused question bank grouped by topic (organization / track record / role / growth / tooling / industry trends). Bring 10–12 options and select the 4–5 that match the manager's introduction.
- Look into the manager's LinkedIn profile for tenure, previous organizations, and public talks. If it arises naturally, reference a particular shared interest; do not manufacture one.
- Prepare in advance for: "what is prompting you to look" and "what would make this position appealing to you."
- Approach the conversation as a mutual evaluation; drifting into excessive deference can signal weak conviction.
